unique_hand_authored.instruction: Tailor your summary to each specific job application.
Keep your summary to 3-4 lines or 50-75 words.
Lead with your strongest qualification or most relevant experience.
Quantify accomplishments whenever possible.
Start each bullet point with a strong action verb.
Focus on results and impact rather than responsibilities.
Prioritize experience most relevant to the target role.
Group skills by category for better readability.
Include relevant coursework, projects, and achievements.
Use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
Include technical keywords relevant to the position.
Order skills by relevance to the target role.
Include project links and technologies used.
Write in third person implied (no 'I' or 'my').
Demonstrate progression and growth in your career.
Include GPA if 3.5 or higher.
Use standard section headings (Summary, Experience, Education, Skills).
Avoid tables, columns, headers, and footers.
Use exact keywords from the job description.
Include both acronyms and full terms.
Use standard fonts (Arial, Calibri, Garamond).
Include job title keywords in your experience bullets.
Every experience bullet should contain at least one metric.
Summary must mention the target role or industry.
Skills section should have 10-15 relevant skills.
Address the hiring manager by name when possible.
Connect your experience directly to the job requirements.
